records.type: Official U.S. & PRC Defense Posture Reports, Force Structure Baselines & 2025 Economic/Military Forecasts
records.description: Documents the 1999 PLA doctrinal shift to 'integrated operations and key point strikes' ('campaigns of paralysis'), the December 2004 PRC Defense White Paper prioritizing the Navy, Air Force, and 2nd Artillery and seating their chiefs on the CMC, the 2006 U.S. QDR Pacific posture (≥6 carriers and 60% of USN submarines), USN vs. PLAN submarine force tables (54 SSNs / 16 SSBNs / 4 SSGNs vs. 5 SSNs / 61 SSKs / 1 SSBN), and the 2005 DoD Report's 2025 GDP projections (U.S. $22.3T, China $6.4T, Japan $6.3T).
records.use_description: The papers compare annual official estimates and policy descriptions. The relevant institutional attribution follows the cited edition.

records.title: U.S. Critical Infrastructure Cyber Policy (EO 13010 to EO 13800), 'Defend Forward' (2018 DoD Cyber Strategy) & USNWC Public-Private Escalation Wargames (NWC-CI17, NWC-DF19)
records.author_org: U.S. Naval War College Center for Cyber Conflict Studies (Jacquelyn Schneider, Benjamin Schechter, Rachael Shaffer) & Cyber and Innovation Policy Institute (CIPI Staff)
records.type: Empirical Cyber Escalation Wargaming, Critical Infrastructure Interdependency & 'Defend Forward' Strategy Analysis
records.description: Combines the 2017 Navy–Private Sector Critical Infrastructure War Game (~125 players, 66 cyber injects across 14 sectors, reporting within the particular exercise that nuclear and cascading Energy/Transportation effects drive national security escalation while private firms resist federal patches and want DoD pre-conflict counter-cyber operations) and the 2019 Defend Forward War Game (>100 players, ~50 finance/electric executives, reporting within the particular exercise that private industry supports counter-cyber capability degradation but opposes mutual-vulnerability attacks on foreign civilian infrastructure).
records.use_description:
The papers use policy documents to trace changes in institutional responsibilities and published games as evidence of research design.

**Interpretive scope.** The reported player responses belong to particular exercises and assumptions. They do not establish a universal causal effect of cyber operations or independently validate later Taiwan scenarios.

records.title: Rear Adm. Michael A. McDevitt's Comprehensive Net Assessment of the PLA Navy: Maritime Power Theory, Overseas Learning Curve & Blue-Water Operations (CN21-C1, CN21-C2, CN21-C3, CN21-C8)
records.author_org: Rear Adm. Michael A. McDevitt, USN (Ret.) (China As a Twenty-First Century Naval Power: Theory, Practice, and Implications, Naval Institute Press, 2020)
records.type: Strategic Naval Net Assessment, Deployment Chronology & Force-Structure Monograph
records.description: Synthesizes McDevitt's 2020 monograph across Hu Jintao's Nov 2012 'maritime great power' (haiyang qiangguo) directive and Xi Jinping's Oct 18, 2017 19th Party Congress 2035/2050 timelines (catching the p. 9 'October 2018' typo in CN21C1-R01); China's 'SLOC anxiety' (8.4M bpd oil imports in 2017, 80–90% seaborne trade, 'blue granary' 2,700+ global fishing fleet); the 1980 DF-5 South Pacific task force, Tables 1 & 2 (1985–2008 overseas deployments), and 12 years of Gulf of Aden antipiracy escorts (33 rotations, 58 warships [43 Type 054As], 27,000 sailors, SHADE, COSCO 2-day emergency purchasing, 2-level flat Beijing C2, Aug 1, 2017 Djibouti base, and 210-day / 100k–120k nm naval diplomacy); and the 131 blue-water warships built since 2004.
records.use_description: The papers use the monograph as a secondary assessment whose comparisons reflect the period and definitions used by the author.

connection_review.finding: CN21-C4 is a selected chapter of McDevitt’s same 2020 monograph. Its scenario should not be labelled an external citation of that monograph.
CN21-C5 is another supplied chapter of the same monograph. Treat it as part of the work, not independent confirmation.
